newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends firm on Yeltsin, FOMC worries.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends firm on Yeltsin, FOMC worries.

text.p: The Swiss franc ended higher and may have room to the upside temporarily, although some analysts see a chance for a slightly higher dollar/Swiss range a bit longer-term.

The dollar/Swiss lost ground on fundamental factors ranging from concerns about Russian President Yeltsin's health, to worries about a possible U.S. rate rise at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting.
Traders said mark/Swiss also suffered from Yeltsin worries. A meeting of European finance ministers in Dublin at the weekend was seen negative on balance for the mark as well.
"The franc is quite strong. The mark is also weak, after coming under pressure from the latest meeting in Dublin," said Thomas Steinemann, analyst at Swiss Volksbank.

The officials agreed that a stability pact was needed to ensure EMU member goverments meet Maastricht Treaty criteria. But they stopped short of agreeing on how such a pact would be enforced with respect to any penalty or similar measures. This weighed on the mark.
Dollar/Swiss was also pressured by weak U.S. securities markets ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC).
Worries about Yeltsin also prompted a flight to quality into the Swiss franc, traders said.
In addition, Steinemann said that comments by SNB board member Bruno Gehrig over the weekend may have added upward momentum to the Swiss franc.
Gehrig said in a speech to foreign exchange traders that monetary policy takes the Swiss franc level into account but efforts to steer its market levels can only be temporary.
Some traders saw his comments as an indication the SNB would not stand in the way of a pronounced rise in the Swiss franc if markets were determined to send the franc higher.

Aurel David, technical currency analyst at Bank Julius Baer, said dollar/Swiss remained in a period of consolidation. But he did not rule out a test of the upside, possibly into a range of 1.2575/2630 in the next 10 days. Very near-term a drop below 1.2330/2335 francs may trigger a drop to 1.2290, but that may be a buying opportunity. Mark/Swiss was seen moving sideways with 81.50 next support. * Dollar ends at 1.2337/2347 Swiss francs compared with 1.2415/2420 at Friday's close. * Mark ends at 81.59/61 Swiss centimes, versus 81.88/91. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
